thread:
maya: Anyone else seeing a bunch of gpu pods stuck in Pending? nodes report free GPU memory but scheduler keeps failing fit predicates.
jon: seen it in us-west2 prod, started ~20m ago. autoscaler didn't spin up new mig nodes.
alisha: `kubectl describe pod` shows: FailedScheduling -> 0/12 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
lee: but `nvidia-smi` on some nodes shows free GPU memory and no running processes for those gpus.
maya: I think it's fragmentation: pods request 1 full GPU but some nodes only have fractional slices reserved by other pods so scheduler can't pack.
jon: cluster-autoscaler logs: "scale-up rejected by quota: vCPU quota exceeded" — autoscaler suggested 3 nodes but control plane couldn't provision.
infra-bot: [autoscaler] Suggested: add 3 nodes to nodepool-gpu-mig-16. Provisioning API response: QUOTA_EXCEEDED for project-redwood-us-west2.
alisha: so two issues: (1) fragmentation on existing nodes causing fit failures, (2) cloud quota preventing scale up.
lee: quick mitigation: can we mark a nodepool with dedicated exclusive-gpu taint and drain low-priority fractional pods to coalesce free GPUs?
maya: we tried cordoning a couple nodes and evicting fractional pods earlier but eviction hit PDBs and caused cascading rollbacks in staging. not safe for prod.
jon: alternative: lower binpacking threshold so scheduler prefers nodes with contiguous free GPUs. but that makes scheduler heuristics more conservative and may increase node count/cost.
/alisha: also noticed that the daemonset that assigns fractional-slice tolerations is mis-labeling some pods as "slice=1/2" rather than explicit mif-slice labels; that blocks them from moving to slice-capable nodes.
sre-oncall: can we temporarily relax the quota or request short-term bump from infra quota owners? we can also change autoscaler to prefer on-demand rather than spot to avoid provisioning wait.
maya: requesting quota bump now, pinging @people-ops infra-quotas.
jon: measured impact: 37 pending pods across 4 deployments, tail latency on inference endpoints increased 4x. cost of immediate fix (add on-demand nodes) ~ $2k/day — ops ask if we should absorb.
lee: suggestion: add a small nodepool with MIG 1g.5g config (smaller slices) to run fractional workloads separately; keep 1:1 whole-gpu pool for latency-critical pods. reduces fragmentation.
alisha: that's the longer-term fix. short term: patch daemonset to correct slice labels so fractional pods can be packed onto slice-capable nodes, then force a rolling restart of those deployments (low-traffic window).
maya: steps: (1) request quota bump (maya) (2) enable temporary on-demand fallback in autoscaler policy (jon) (3) patch daemonset and roll fractional workloads (alisha + lee) (4) create plan for new MIG slice-only nodepool (sre-oncall + eng-planning).
jon: I'll flip autoscaler policy and monitor. will post logs.
infra-bot: [action] quota_bump_request 1922004801 created by maya.
maya: thanks — i'll update when infra approves. :thumbsup:
lee: any objections to doing the daemonset patch during the 00:00-02:00 UTC window tonight?
sre-oncall: that's acceptable. I'll stand by and roll back if we see errors.
jon: FYI after flipping autoscaler to on-demand fallback, we saw provisioning succeed for 1 node (1922004820), but it didn't show up ready for ~3m due to CNI attach race. patch queued.
maya: ok let's keep this thread for updates. will paste follow-ups here.
jon: paste of failing scheduler binds (from kube-scheduler log): ```I0305 03:12:41.123456 1 predicate_checker.go:123] Pod default/model-a: Fit failed: Insufficient= nvidia.com/gpu(12); Node node-gpu-42: allocatable=1, requested=2; fragmentationScore=0.78```
alisha: noted. fragmentationScore > 0.7 suggests we should tighten fragmentation-aware binpacker.
maya: next update in 15m with quota status.
